children: Willdan Group agreed to acquire Mantis Intermediate Holdings, a Texas-based building controls company, for $285 million in cash.

The technical services company said the addition of Mantis will expand its presence in industries including data centers, healthcare, and food and beverage. The deal is expected to be accretive to Willdan's earnings in 2027.

The transaction is expected to be funded by a new $250 million term loan facility, Willdan said Tuesday, adding that it has already received an underwritten financing commitment. The company's cash on hand and borrowings under existing credit facilities will also partially fund the deal.

"This addition significantly strengthens our energy procurement offering, industrial energy efficiency business, and positions Willdan for the growing demand of new energy-efficient data centers," Chief Executive Officer Mike Bieber said.
Mantis is expected to generate $120 million of net revenue this year, with an adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization margin in the low 20s, Bieber said.
The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter, subject to completion of the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust approval process.
